PHP309 | #Skinfluenced: Decoding Skincare for Clinical Impact, Fall 2026 Change Title (3 crs.) This elective course aims to enhance students' knowledge of adjunctive therapies for dermatological conditions. Beginning with an introduction to adjunctive therapies, skincare ingredients, and skin types, the course will focus on non-prescription treatments for common dermatological conditions such as acne vulgaris, atopic dermatitis, seborrheic dermatitis, hyperpigmentation, rosacea, and xerosis. Students will utilize primary literature and guidelines to develop treatment plans, compare and contrast available products, and identify and respond to medical misinformation regarding various dermatological concerns. FOR CONFIRMATION BY THE FACULTY SENATE NEW PROGRAM COLLEGE OF EDUCATION: BA-Learning and Education in Action,Fall2026 Appendix A Learning happens all aroundus-not exclusively in traditional school settings.This flexible degree teaches pedagogical development in varied community,industry,and organizational learning spaces.
Participants in this education degree program will develop essential skills and competencies Based Learning;2.) Meeting the Needs of Diverse Populations Locally and Globally,3.)Adapted Physical Education, and 4.) Student Defined.
Graduates of this program will be prepared to foster effective learning across a range of settings using innovative and inclusive approaches to learning experience design.

Curricular Matters Which Require Confirmation By The Faculty Senate COURSE CHANGES COLLEGE OF EDUCATION EDP 630 | Issues in Educational Leadership Policy and Analysis, Effective Fall 2026 Change course title and/or course description, change in method of instruction, change prerequisites (3 crs.) Explores U.S. education policy and governance, examining governmental and nongovernmental actors, policy processes, and cultural forces.
Develops analytical skills and frameworks to evaluate competing interests, institutional complexity, and ethical considerations across K–20 systems. (Lec. 3/Online) COLLEGE OF ENGINEERING CHE 543 | Electrochemical Energy Storage-Fundamentals and Applications, Effective Fall 2026 Change course title and/or course description, change in method of instruction (3 crs.) Electric vehicles, energy generated by solar and wind and portable electronic devices are powered by batteries.

Electrochemistry thermodynamics and kinetics are at the heart of all batteries.
Electrochemistry fundamentals and emerging applications will be reviewed in this class.
Demonstrations and projects will include battery fabrication, characterization and modeling of single cells as well as battery management systems. (Lec. 3) Pre: CHE213 or MCE341 (or equivalent) and undergraduate course in thermodynamics.
Or by permission of instructor.
GRADUATE SCHOOL OF OCEANOGRAPHY OCG 528 | High-Temperature Geochemistry, Effective Fall 2026 Change course title and/or course description, change course level, change prerequisites (3 crs.) Principles and factors governing the distribution of trace elements in volcanic processes.
Applications to the study of rock genesis, mantle dynamics, oceanic crust formation, and hotspots. (Lec. 3) Pre: Permission of instructor.

OCG 582 | Geophysical Fluid Dynamics I, Effective Fall 2026 Change course title and/or course description, change course number, change prerequisites (3 crs.) Natural world ﬂ uid dynamics emphasizing ocean circulation.
Classical ﬂ uid dynamics; GFD fundamentals (rotation and strati ﬁ cation); Taylor-Proudman theorem; potential vorticity; planetary waves; geostrophic contours; shallow water quasi-geostrophic theory; frictional layers. (Lec. 3) Pre: EGR515 or permission of instructor.
NEW COURSES COLLEGE OF ARTS AND SCIENCES AAF 409 | Afro-Caribbean Culture: History, Identity, Global Influence, Effective Fall 2026 (3 crs.) Examine Afro-Caribbean traditions through culture, identity, and exchange.
Explore African heritage, colonialism, migration, and indigenous influences shaping dance, religion, festivals, and expressions of resistance, resilience, and creativity across global cultures. (Lec. 3) Pre: Minimum sophomore standing.
COLLEGE OF EDUCATION EDC 446 | Perspectives on “Glocal” Education, Effective Spring 2026 (3 crs.) Our world is increasingly interconnected.

To make sense of the dynamic forces and stakeholders shaping educational experiences, practices, issues, and beliefs, we will explore these facets through a glocalized lens.
Mannion (2015) calls upon us to consider the following question: “What if education can only address so-called global concerns through the local—contextualized in some ‘place’? (p. 21).
Using the 17 UNESCO Sustainability Goals as a framework of consideration, we will explore the global and local mediators to equitable and inclusive education. (Lec. 3/Online) (C2) (D1) Pre: Sophomore standing.
EDC 492 | Literacies and Learning in Place, Effective Fall 2026 (3 crs.) Explore how space and place shape learning and literacy.
Examine neighborhoods, classrooms, and public sites to design equitable, community-grounded experiences that foster creativity, connection, and critical engagement through readings, fieldwork, and projects. (Seminar) Pre: LEiA program major or permission of instructor.

EDC 550 | Advancing Learning with Technology in Health Professions Ed, Effective Spring 2027 (3 crs.) Explores strategies for teaching adults using technology in health professions education, including online platforms, simulation, small-group facilitation, interprofessional approaches, and emerging tools such as AI to improve learning outcomes. (Accelerated Online Program) Pre: Admitted to the College of Education.
EDC 551 | Leadership and Innovation in Health Professions Education, Effective Fall 2026 (3 crs.) This course explores leadership and innovation in medical education, focusing on collaboration, creativity, technology, and equity to improve teaching, learning, and organizational change across health professions. (Accelerated Online Program) Pre: Admitted to the College of Education.
EDD 600 | Change Leadership and Systems Improvement, Effective Fall 2026 (3 crs.) All leadership is change leadership, and the ability to guide transformation across diverse contexts is a critical skill for today’s leaders.
This course examines the theories, practices, and tools of leading change in complex educational and organizational systems.

Students will study adaptive and technical change, systems thinking, and continuous improvement methodologies, with an emphasis on how leaders create the conditions for sustainable organizational learning, equity-driven change, and systemic improvement. (Online) Pre: Admission to EdD program or permission of instructor.

EDD 601 | Data, Decision & Implementation Science in Education, Effective Fall 2026 (3 crs.)This course prepares scholar–practitioners to diagnose educational problems, make evidence-informed decisions, and implement improvement at the classroom, school, district, or system level. We blend decision science, implementation science, and equity-centered leadership to help you design and test practical changes that work in your context. (Online) Pre: EDP612, EDP613, and enrolled in the EdD Program, or by permission of instructor. S/U or Letter Grades. EDD 697 | Doctoral Praxis Project I, Effective Fall 2026 (3 crs.) Prepares Ed.D. students to develop a Doctoral Praxis Project proposal. Frames problems of practice, analyzes context, defines leadership role, and proposes actions and timeline for meaningful, sustain able organizational change. (Online) Pre: Admission to EdD program or permission of instructor. EDD 698 | Doctoral Praxis Project II, Effective Fall 2026 (2 crs.) Supports Ed.D. students in enacting and presenting the Doctoral Praxis Project. Focuses on project implementation, progress reporting, artifact development, and dissemination through internal and external presentations. (Online) Pre: EDC697, and Admission to EdD program. May be repeated for a total of 6 credits.

COURSES CASC Bill 2025-2026-04A At the January 6, 2026 meeting of the Curriculum & Standards Committee, the following matters were considered and are now presented to the Faculty Senate for approval. INFORMATIONAL MATTERS COURSES FORWARD TO THE GRADUATE COUNCIL FOR REVIEW: BUS401 | Global Topics in Business: Career Accelerator JOR490 | Community News Lab FOR CONFIRMATION BY THE FACULTY SENATE NEW COURSES COLLEGE OF BUSINESS: INE347 | Entrepreneurial Accounting and Finance, effective Fall 2026 (3 crs.) Topics focus on the principles of new venture accounting and finance. Accounting topics include assessing the health of a new venture, and cash and other financial planning for the smaller enterprise. Finance topics include introduction to start u p issues such as raising seed and growth capital from founders, grants, venture capitalists and angels, investment banking, commercial banking, bootstrapping sources, entrepreneurship through acquisition, and understanding audiences of financial statements and issues unique to small and medium-sized firms. We will also investigate sources of new venture support found both locally and nationally. (Lec. 3) Pre: Junior standing. COLLEGE OF EDUCATION: EDC475 | Early Childhood Practical Teaching Residency 1 Seminar, effective Fall 2026 (3 crs.) This seminar course offers professional support for the early Childhood Practical teaching Residency. This includes dialogue, reflection, goal setting, and teaching analysis during fall residency

and is conducted by a clinical educator and a university supervisor.
Focus will be on developing practices in classroom and behavior management, and assessment to meet the needs of a diverse range of learners, and to help students become reflective and intentional early childhood educators. (Lec. 2, Seminar 1) Pre: Concurrent enrollment in EDC350 and EDC474, admission to College of Education; Admission to the Early Childhood Certification Program; Admission to the Early Childhood Care and Education for Working Professionals; or permission of the instructor.
Not for graduate credit.
COLLEGE OF THE ENVIRONMENT AND LIFE SCIENCES: BIO380 | The Ecology of Iceland and the North Atlantic, effective Summer 2026 (3 crs.) Survey of North Atlantic coastal and oceanic habitats via field experience in Iceland, with emphasis on ecology and fisheries.
Travel required; additional costs apply. (Lec. 3) Pre: BIO260 or BIO262, or by permission of instructor GEO380 | Geology of Iceland, effective Summer 2026 (3 crs.) Explores physical geology in an off-campus field experience in Iceland with a focus on sustainable geosciences in a changing climate.

Travel required; additional costs apply. (Lec. 1, Seminar) Pre: 200-level course in GEO or permission of instructor.
COLLEGE OF NURSING: NUR200 | Nurse Wellbeing & Resilience, effective Fall 2026 (1 cr.) Introduces nursing students to wellness and resiliency concepts emphasizing self-care, stress management, emotional intelligence, and mindfulness to promote personal well-being, professional balance, and sustainable nursing practice through reflective, evidence-based learning. (Lec. 1) Pre: Credit with a minimum grade of C in BIO222, BIO223, CMB201, CHM103, and NUR100.
NUR204 | Pathopharmacology I, effective Fall 2026 (3 crs.) Examine pathophysiology and pharmacology principles for nurses, emphasizing concepts and rationales essential for clinical decision-making and the care of individuals with select diseases across the lifespan. (Lec. 3) Pre: Credit with a minimum grade of C in BIO222, BIO223, CMB201, CHM103, and NUR100.

NUR205 | Pathopharmacology II, effective Fall 2026 (3 crs.) Examine pathophysiology and pharmacology principles for nurses, emphasizing concepts and rationales essential for clinical decision-making and the care of individuals with select diseases across the lifespan, part B. (Lec. 3) Pre: Credit with a minimum grade of C in BIO222, BIO223, CMB201, CHM103, and NUR100.
NUR458 | Comprehensive Care Across the Lifespan & Settings, effective Fall 2026 (3 crs.) Care of individuals and families across the lifespan and settings with complex illnesses, emphasizing client and family responses, empowering self-care, and maximizing quality of life. (Lec. 3) Pre: Credit with a minimum grade of C in NUR333, NUR334, NUR353, NUR354 and NUR413.
Not for graduate credit,

COURSE MODIFICATIONS COLLEGE OF ARTS & SCIENCES: ART243 | Sculpture I: Making the Object, effective Fall 2026 Change credits, prerequisites, title (4 crs.) Formation of three-dimensional forms employing basic sculptural materials and techniques.
Basic media, emphasis on form, material, and structural means in studio practice. (Studio) ART315 | Photography II: Contemporary Photography Practice, effective Fall 2026 Change title, credits, description, prerequisites, repeat criteria (4 crs.) Expand your photography skills to visually communicate creatively through photography and imaging while engaging with contemporary practices.
Photo II emphasizes experimentation, printing and installation. (Studio) Pre: ART214.
May be taken up to two times.
ART332 | Print Media II: Contemporary Print Practice, effective Fall 2026 Change title, description, repeat criteria, prerequisites (4 crs.) Students expand printmaking through relief, monotype, bookmaking, risograph, and digital methods while engaging global print cultures and contemporary practices. (Studio) Pre: ART231.
May be repeated for up to 8 credits.

JOR445 | Special Topics in Journalism, effective Fall 2026 Change repeat criteria (3 crs.) Subject, course content, and years offered will vary according to expertise and availability of instructors. (Lecture/Lab./Seminar) Pre: permission of instructor.
May be repeated for credit with different topic, up to 5 times.
Not for graduate credit.
COLLEGE OF BUSINESS: BAI109 | Business Computing and Quantitative Analysis, effective Fall 2026 Change prerequisites (3 crs.) Applications, concepts, and skills relevant to technology and quantitative processes in business.
Topics include financial analysis, business modeling, and spreadsheets that promote effective decision making.
MS Excel certification exam preparation. (Lec. 3) Pre: Open to students with a BU code earning a C- or better in MTH101, or by permission of the instructor.
FIN436X | Real Estate Development and Finance, effective Summer 2026 Add online modality to existing in-person course (3 crs.) The study of real estate development and finance with a focus on acquisition, finance, market analysis, design, and construction. (Lec. 3/Online) Pre: FIN220 or FIN323, or permission of instructor.
Not for graduate credit.

MKT265 | Marketing Principles, effective Summer 2026 Modify prerequisites (3 crs.) An introduction to marketing from a managerial viewpoint.
Examines social, economic, technological, legal, ethical, and other environmental factors and their impact on product, price, promotion, and distribution decisions in a worldwide market. (Lec. 3/Online) Pre: Open to students with 24 credits or permission of dean's office.
COLLEGE OF EDUCATION: EDC316 | Foundations in Early Childhood Care & Education, effective Summer 2026 Change prerequisites, add accelerated online version (3 crs.) This foundational course prepares aspiring early childhood educators to develop their teaching philosophy, skills, and practices aligned with educational theories.
It emphasizes career exploration and commitment to the profession, promoting optimal learning for young children. (Lec. 3/Online/Accelerated Online Program) Pre: Admission to the College of Education or the Early Childhood Education Program, or Admission to the accelerated online early childhood care and education program, or by permission of instructor.

EDC474 | Early Childhood Practical Teaching Residency I, effective Fall 2026 Change title, description, number/level, credits, add accelerated online version (3 cr.) Students complete their initial residency experience in a public school PreK–3 classroom, attending two full days per week prior to Residency II.
Provides guided field experience supported by a clinical educator and a university supervisor.
Candidates apply developmentally appropriate practices, strengthen classroom management and assessment skills, and engage in reflective teaching to prepare for full-time student teaching in Residency II. (Practicum/Online/Accelerated Online Program) Pre: Concurrent enrollment in EDC426 and EDC475, Admission to College of Education; Admission to the Early Childhood Certification Program; Admission to the Early Childhood Care and Education for Working Professionals; or permission of the instructor.
S/U only.
COLLEGE OF NURSING: NUR203 | Comprehensive Health Assessment, effective Summer 2026 Change prerequisites (3 crs.) Introduces the techniques of history taking and systematic health assessment of individuals across the life span.

Recognition of normal findings is emphasized. (Lec. 2, Lab. 3) Pre: Credit with a minimum grade of C in BIO222, BIO223, CMB201, CHM103, and NUR100.
NUR208 | Growth, Development, & Health Promotion Across the Lifespan, effective Fall 2026 Change prerequisites (3 crs.) Comprehensive understanding of human growth and development throughout the lifespan with an emphasis on health promotion for clients living with/without disabilities and chronic illness. (Lec. 3/Online) Pre: Credit with a minimum grade of C in BIO222, BIO223, CMB201, CHM103, and NUR100.

NUR233 | Introduction to Care of Adults and Older Adults, effective Spring 2027 Change prerequisites (3 crs.) Introduction to foundational nursing practice involving adults and older adults.
Focus on prevention, collaborative care and nursing management of clients' responses to common disorders and health issues in these populations. (Lec. 3) Pre: Credit with a minimum grade of C in NUR203, NUR208, and NUR204 or NUR205, and concurrent enrollment in NUR234.
NUR234 | Practicum: Care of Adults and Older Adults, effective Spring 2027 Change prerequisites (3 crs.) Practicum emphasizing foundational nursing practice focusing on the adult and older adult with acute and chronic illnesses. (Lab. 3) Pre: Credit with a minimum grade of C in NUR203, NUR208, and NUR204 or NUR205, and concurrent enrollment in NUR233.
NUR253 | Nursing Inquiry, effective Spring 2028 Change title, description, prerequisites (3 crs.) Introduction to nursing research, evidenced-based practice, and quality improvement.
Develop understanding of the impact of these principles on nursing care and patient outcomes. (Lec: 3) Pre: Credit with a minimum grade of C in STA220, NUR313 and NUR314.

NUR313 | Acute Care of Adults and Older Adults, effective Fall 2027 Change prerequisites (3 crs.) Nursing management of adults and older adults with acute illness, emphasizing nursing strategies based on a collaborative care model. (Lab. 3) Pre: Credit with a minimum grade of C in NUR233, NUR234, NUR204 and NUR205 and concurrent enrollment in NUR314.
NUR314 | Practicum: Clients with Acute and Chronic Illnesses, effective Fall 2027 Change prerequisites (3 crs.) Application of nursing strategies in the management of clients with acute and chronic illness, including the impact on their families. (Lab. 3) Pre: Credit with a minimum grade of C in NUR233, NUR234, NUR204 and NUR205.
Concurrent enrollment in NUR313.
NUR333 | Psychiatric Mental Health Nursing, effective Spring 2028 Change prerequisites (3 crs.) Incorporating an integrated biological, psychological, socio-cultural, environmental, and spiritual approach, this course emphasizes knowledge needed to care for individuals with a psychiatric disorder, and their families/caregivers, across the care continuum. (Lec. 3) Pre: Credit with a minimum grade of C in NUR313, NUR314, NUR443, NUR444 concurrent enrollment in NUR334.

NUR334 | Practicum: Psychiatric Mental Health Nursing, effective Spring 2028 Change prerequisites, modify lab hours (3 crs.) This clinical course provides students with the opportunity to apply theoretical knowledge of psychiatric mental health nursing through supervised experience in diverse clinical settings. (Lab. 9) Pre: Credit with a minimum grade of C in NUR313, NUR314, NUR443 and NUR444.
Concurrent enrollment in NUR333.

NUR353 | Family Health Nursing, effective Spring 2028 Change prerequisites, description, credits (3 crs.) This course focuses on the care of families, including children, child-bearing individuals, and caregivers, applying clinical judgment with awareness of social, economic, environmental, and cultural factors impact on health. (Lec. 3) Pre: Credit with a minimum grade of C in NUR313, NUR314, NUR443, NUR444 and concurrent enrollment in NUR354.
NUR354 | Practicum in Family Health Nursing, effective Spring 2028 Change prerequisites, title, description, lab hours (3 crs.) This practicum focuses on providing care to families, including children, child-bearing individuals, and caregivers, and applying clinical judgment with awareness of social, economic, environmental, and cultural factors impact on health. (Lab. 9) Pre: Credit with a minimum grade of C in NUR313, NUR314, NUR443, NUR444 and concurrent enrollment in NUR353.
NUR412 | Health Care Economics, Policy, & Transition to Practice, effective Spring 2029 Change prerequisites, title, description (3 crs.) Explores healthcare economics, policy, and professional transition to practice.

Emphasizes ethical decision-making, leadership, and advocacy to prepare nurses for complex, evolving healthcare systems and interdisciplinary collaboration. (Lec. 3) Pre: Credit with a minimum grade of C in NUR333, NUR334, NUR353, NUR354 and NUR413.
Not for graduate credit.
NUR413 | Complex Care of Adults and Older Adults, effective Fall 2028 Change prerequisites (3 crs.) Nursing management of clients with complex and critical illnesses, with a focus on the client and family responses to illness, empowering self-care management and maximizing quality of life. (Lec. 3) Pre: Credit with a C or better in NUR253; NUR333; NUR334 or NUR 353; and NUR354.
Not for graduate credit.
NUR417 | Clinical Immersion, effective Spring 2029 Change prerequisites, credits (6 crs.) Designed to provide students with the opportunity to comprehensively apply and integrate synthesized theoretical and clinical experiences from previous nursing courses into the final comprehension clinical experience. (Lab. 6) Pre: Credit with a minimum grade of C or better in NUR333, NUR334, NUR353, NUR354 and NUR413.
Not for graduate credit.

NUR444 | Practicum: Population Health Nursing, effective Fall 2027 Change prerequisites, title, description (3 crs.) This practicum provides experience applying population health concepts.
Students will identify health disparities and impact of social determinants of health while using community-based interventions to promote population-wide well-being. (Lab. 9) Pre: Credit with a minimum grade of C in NUR233, NUR234, NUR204 and NUR205.
Concurrent enrollment in NUR443.
Not for graduate credit. (D1) (C1)

FACULTY SENATE OFFICE 224 P ASTORE H ALL , 51 L OWER C OLLEGE R OAD , K INGSTON , R I 02881 U SA , P: 401.874.2616 Faculty Senate Resolution 2025-2026-01 Resolution of Appreciation and Gratitude Honoring Kent and Diane Fannon WHEREAS , Kent and Diane Fannon, distinguished alumni of the University of Rhode Island, Class of 1974, have made a profound and lasting impact on the University through their longtime support of the University of Rhode Island; and WHEREAS , the Fannon’s previous gifts, including direct scholarships for students, endowed support for the College of Business, and establishment of the Diane and Kent Fannon Education Research Endowment, have already made a significant impact on the University and its students; and WHEREAS , the University College for Academic Success has evolved into a dynamic center for student community and support under the visionary leadership of founding Dean Emerita Jayne Richmond and current Executive Director Kim Stack; and WHEREAS , the Fannon’s commitment to student achievement, career readiness, and holistic support have now propelled the launch of the Fannon Institute for Student Success, which will transform the University College for Academic Success with revitalized and modernized programming; and WHEREAS , the new Fannon Institute for Student Success will bring together, under one administrative umbrella, five key areas of student support: Career and Experiential Education, Academic Enhancement, Retention, Exploratory Advising, and Student-Athlete Support Services; and WHEREAS , creation of the Fannon Institute for Student Success will transform the student experience, ensuring that every student has access to the tools, mentorship, and resources to succeed; and, finally, WHEREAS , Kent and Diane Fannon’s extraordinary generosity is a testament to their unwavering belief in the power of education and their desire to leave a legacy that will inspire future generations; NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED , that the Faculty Senate of the University of Rhode Island, on behalf of the entire General Faculty, expresses its profound appreciation and heartfelt gratitude to the Fannon Family for their visionary generosity, their enduring legacy of support for URI students, and their commitment to ensuring that generations of students will have the tools and resources they need to achieve their highest ambitions; and BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED , that this resolution be entered into the official minutes of the Faculty Senate and that a copy be sent to Kent and Diane Fannon as a token of our deep appreciation.

Unanimously adopted this Twentieth day of November in the year Two Thousand and Twenty-Five. ________________________________________ _________________________________________ Travis D.
Williams, URI Faculty Senate President Marc B.
Parlange, University President

Constitution, By-Laws and University Manual Committee CBUM Informational/Editorial Report #2025-2026-01 January 22, 2026 Faculty Senate Meeting (Approved by CBUM 1/15/26 ) Editorial change: Removes ‘and Providence Plantations’ from the state name.
Rhode Island’s state name changed in 2020 and this outdated reference is being corrected.
Existing Language: 6.10.10 Policy Statement on Freedom of Expression.
Faith in the fundamental importance of freedom forms a major theme in the history, government and tradition of the State of Rhode Island and Providence Plantations and of the United States of America.
Freedom is also recognized on practical grounds as vital to scholars in their search for and dissemination of truth.
Although academic freedom is not written into law, it is well established in custom and grounded in traditions of long standing in the colleges and universities of the Western world, protecting professional scholars and teachers from interference with their obligation to pursue truth.

Though it is a specific kind of freedom peculiar to members of the teaching profession in higher education, its benefits ultimately accrue as much to the public at large as to the scholars themselves.
In fact, the present age of accelerating change emphasizes that education must stress development of the capacity for critical thought, a capacity that can be achieved only when freedom in inquiry and discussion prevail.
Therefore, in accordance with the ideals of state and nation, and in order that the institutions under its jurisdiction might perform well the functions for which they are established, the former Board of Trustees of State Colleges affirmed its unqualified acceptance of the principle of freedom in inquiry and expression. #21-22-6 Proposed Language: 6.10.10 Policy Statement on Freedom of Expression.
